objects.definition: typedef struct RGFW_info RGFW_info;
objects.description: Opaque handle to the global RGFW instance and state. Forward-declared here; full definition appears when RGFW_NATIVE or RGFW_IMPLEMENTATION is used. Used to initialize, configure, and query library-wide state.

objects.definition: typedef struct RGFW_window RGFW_window;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a window object used for creating and managing a platform window and its input/events. Forward-declared here; full definition appears under RGFW_NATIVE/IMPLEMENTATION.

objects.definition: typedef struct RGFW_window_src RGFW_window_src;
objects.description: Opaque handle to the platform-specific window source (Win32/Wayland/X11/Cocoa). Forward-declared here; full definition is provided under RGFW_NATIVE/IMPLEMENTATION. Retrieved from an RGFW_window for low-level interop.

objects.definition: typedef struct RGFW_nativeImage RGFW_nativeImage;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a platform-native image wrapper used by software surfaces (e.g., XImage, HBITMAP, wl_buffer). Forward-declared in the API; defined under RGFW_NATIVE/IMPLEMENTATION.

objects.definition: typedef struct RGFW_surface RGFW_surface;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a software-rendered surface with pixel data and a native backing. Forward-declared here; full struct is defined under RGFW_NATIVE/IMPLEMENTATION.

objects.definition: typedef void RGFW_mouse;
objects.description: Opaque mouse cursor/icon handle. Platform-specific pointer for setting a custom cursor on a window.
Enumeration of pixel formats for images/surfaces. Underlying type is u8; ptr_type reflects the typedef name form requirement.

objects.definition: typedef RGFW_ENUM(u8, RGFW_key) { ... };
objects.description: Enumeration of abstract keyboard keys used by RGFW. Underlying type is u8. Contains ASCII-like values and extended keys (F1.., arrows, keypad, etc.).
Enumeration of mouse button codes. Underlying type u8.
Bitmask enumeration of key modifier states (caps, num, ctrl, alt, shift, super, scroll). Underlying type u8.

objects.definition: typedef RGFW_ENUM(u8, RGFW_eventType) { ... };
objects.description: Enumeration of event types emitted by RGFW (keyboard, mouse, window, drag-and-drop, DPI, quit, etc.). Underlying type u8.

objects.definition: typedef RGFW_ENUM(u32, RGFW_eventFlag) { ... };
objects.description: Bitmask enumeration that enables/disables groups of events and convenience combinations (all, key, mouse, window, focus, data drop). Underlying type u32.
Common header for all events: type and target window pointer. Embedded in other event structs.
Event data for mouse button press/release.
Event data for mouse scroll (x, y delta).
Event data for mouse motion, including position and raw vector.
Event data for keyboard press/release, including physical key, mapped char, repeat flag, and modifiers.
Event data for file drops: files array and count.
Event data for drag-in-progress with position.
Event data for content scale (DPI) updates on a window.
Tagged union for all RGFW events. First member is type for quick inspection.
Enum for event waiting behavior when polling (no wait or wait for next). Underlying type i32.

objects.definition: typedef RGFW_ENUM(u32, RGFW_windowFlags) { ... };
objects.description: Bitmask flags controlling window creation and behaviors (border, resize, DnD, fullscreen, transparency, raw mouse, OpenGL/EGL, etc.). Underlying type u32.
Target locations to set window icon (taskbar, window, or both). Underlying type u8.

objects.definition: typedef RGFW_ENUM(u8, RGFW_mouseIcons) { ... };
objects.description: Standard system cursor icons enumeration. Underlying type u8.
Flash/attention request types for a window. Underlying type u8.
Debug message severity kinds. Underlying type u8.

objects.definition: typedef RGFW_ENUM(u8, RGFW_errorCode) { ... };
objects.description: Error/info codes for various subsystems (OpenGL/EGL, Wayland/X11, DirectX, clipboard, buffers, events, etc.). Underlying type u8.
Monitor mode descriptor including resolution, refresh rate, and RGB bit depths. Used when requesting/compare modes.
Monitor information (work area position, name, content scale, pixel ratio, physical size, current mode).
Bitmask describing which monitor mode fields to consider/apply when changing or comparing modes. Underlying type u8.
Hint for context release behavior (flush pipeline or none).
OpenGL API profile hint (core, forward-compatible, compatibility, or GLES).
Renderer type hint (hardware-accelerated GPU vs. software).

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_windowMovedfunc)(RGFW_window* win, i32 x, i32 y);
objects.description: Callback type for window move events.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_windowResizedfunc)(RGFW_window* win, i32 w, i32 h);
objects.description: Callback type for window resize events.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_windowRestoredfunc)(RGFW_window* win, i32 x, i32 y, i32 w, i32 h);
objects.description: Callback type for window restore events.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_windowMaximizedfunc)(RGFW_window* win, i32 x, i32 y, i32 w, i32 h);
objects.description: Callback type for window maximized events.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_windowMinimizedfunc)(RGFW_window* win);
objects.description: Callback type for window minimized events.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_windowQuitfunc)(RGFW_window* win);
objects.description: Callback type for window quit events.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_focusfunc)(RGFW_window* win, RGFW_bool inFocus);
objects.description: Callback type for focus-in/out events.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_mouseNotifyfunc)(RGFW_window* win, i32 x, i32 y, RGFW_bool status);
objects.description: Callback type for mouse enter/leave notifications.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_mousePosfunc)(RGFW_window* win, i32 x, i32 y, float vecX, float vecY);
objects.description: Callback type for mouse movement.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_dataDragfunc)(RGFW_window* win, i32 x, i32 y);
objects.description: Callback type for data drag events.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_windowRefreshfunc)(RGFW_window* win);
objects.description: Callback type for window refresh requests.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_keyfunc)(RGFW_window* win, u8 key, u8 sym, RGFW_keymod mod, RGFW_bool repeat, RGFW_bool pressed);
objects.description: Callback type for key press/release.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_mouseButtonfunc)(RGFW_window* win, RGFW_mouseButton button, RGFW_bool pressed);
objects.description: Callback type for mouse button press/release.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_mouseScrollfunc)(RGFW_window* win, float x, float y);
objects.description: Callback type for mouse scroll.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_dataDropfunc)(RGFW_window* win, char** files, size_t count);
objects.description: Callback type for file drop events.

objects.definition: typedef void (* RGFW_scaleUpdatedfunc)(RGFW_window* win, float scaleX, float scaleY);
objects.description: Callback type for monitor DPI/scale updates.

objects.definition: typedef void (*RGFW_proc)(void);
objects.description: Generic function pointer type for procedure addresses (e.g., OpenGL).

functions.name: XDL_init
functions.description: Initializes the XDL loader and dynamically loads the X11 (and optionally GLX and Xrandr) shared libraries, resolving function pointers used elsewhere in the program.
requirements: Call once before using any X11/GLX functions that are provided via XDL.
On Unix-like systems, expects libX11; optionally libGLX/libGL and libXrandr if not disabled by compile-time macros.
No arguments; has global side effects (fills XDL_module[*] and function pointer globals).

functions.name: XDL_close
functions.description: Unloads dynamically loaded X11/GLX/Xrandr libraries previously loaded by XDL_init and clears their module handles.
requirements: Only call after XDL_init has successfully run.
Do not use any X11/GLX functions resolved by XDL after calling this; function pointers become invalid.

functions.name: RGFW_alloc
functions.description: Allocates a block of memory of the requested size using the allocator configured at compile time (RGFW_ALLOC, defaults to malloc).
requirements: size may be zero; behavior follows the underlying allocator.
Caller owns the returned pointer and must free it with RGFW_free.

functions.name: RGFW_free
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated by RGFW_alloc (or the configured RGFW_ALLOC) using the configured deallocator (RGFW_FREE, defaults to free).
requirements: ptr may be NULL (no-op per C free semantics).
Must only be used on pointers returned by RGFW_alloc/RGFW APIs that document RGFW_FREE ownership.

functions.name: RGFW_sizeofWindow
functions.description: Returns sizeof(RGFW_window). Useful for allocations or language bindings.

functions.name: RGFW_sizeofWindowSrc
functions.description: Returns sizeof(RGFW_window_src).

functions.name: RGFW_useWayland
functions.description: Toggles RGFW's use of Wayland on Unix platforms. Sets the global preference used by backends.
requirements: Should be called before creating windows; it calls RGFW_init() implicitly if needed.
Only meaningful on Unix platforms that support Wayland.
Passing non-zero enables Wayland preference; zero requests X11.

functions.name: RGFW_usingWayland
functions.description: Returns whether RGFW is currently using Wayland (true) or not.
requirements: Depends on initialization state and platform availability.

functions.name: RGFW_getLayer_OSX
functions.description: macOS: Retrieves a CAMetalLayer object pointer for use as a rendering layer when creating EGL/WebGPU surfaces.
requirements: Only meaningful on macOS.
Returned pointer is owned by Cocoa; do not free.

functions.name: RGFW_getDisplay_X11
functions.description: X11: Returns the Display* handle for the current RGFW context, or NULL on non-X11 builds.
requirements: Valid only after RGFW_init on X11.
Return type is Display* but typed as void* for portability; cast as needed.

functions.name: RGFW_getDisplay_Wayland
functions.description: Wayland: Returns the wl_display* handle for the current RGFW context, or NULL if Wayland is not active.
requirements: Valid only after RGFW_init on Wayland-enabled builds.

functions.name: RGFW_setClassName
functions.description: Sets the window class name used for grouping windows by the window manager (X11/Win32).
requirements: Call before creating windows to affect their class name.
name must be a null-terminated string; pointer must remain valid until after first window creation on some platforms.

functions.name: RGFW_setXInstName
functions.description: X11: Sets the instance name (res_name) used by X11 resource manager and WM matching.
requirements: Only meaningful on X11; no-op elsewhere.
If used, call before window creation.

functions.name: RGFW_moveToMacOSResourceDir
functions.description: macOS: Changes the current working directory to the app bundle’s Resources directory.
requirements: Only meaningful on macOS.
Call early if your app expects CWD-based resource loading.

functions.name: RGFW_copyImageData
functions.signature: void RGFW_copyImageData(u8* dest_data, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_format dest_format, u8* src_data, RGFW_format src_format)
functions.description: Converts and copies pixel data from src_data in src_format to dest_data in dest_format for an image of size w×h. Handles channel order and alpha filling.
requirements: dest_data and src_data must be non-NULL and point to sufficiently large buffers.
w and h must be positive.
Formats must be valid RGFW_format enumerants.

functions.name: RGFW_sizeofNativeImage
functions.description: Returns sizeof(RGFW_nativeImage).

functions.name: RGFW_sizeofSurface
functions.description: Returns sizeof(RGFW_surface).

functions.name: RGFW_createSurface
functions.signature: RGFW_surface* RGFW_createSurface(u8* data, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_format format)
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an RGFW_surface for software blitting from a raw pixel buffer of given dimensions and format. Backend-specific native image resources are prepared.
requirements: data must reference at least w*h*(channels) bytes; channels depend on format (3 or 4).
w and h must be positive.
Caller must free with RGFW_surface_free.

functions.name: RGFW_createSurfacePtr
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_createSurfacePtr(u8* data, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_format format, RGFW_surface* surface)
functions.description: Initializes a caller-provided RGFW_surface with the given raw pixel buffer for software blitting. Creates native image resources appropriate for the current backend.
requirements: surface must be a valid, writable pointer.
data must be large enough for w*h pixels in the stated format.
w and h must be positive.
Returns RGFW_TRUE on success, RGFW_FALSE on failure.

functions.name: RGFW_surface_getNativeImage
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the native-image sub-structure inside a surface for backend-specific access (e.g., XImage, wl_buffer, HBITMAP).
requirements: surface must be non-NULL.

functions.name: RGFW_surface_free
functions.description: Frees an RGFW_surface created by RGFW_createSurface, including any internal/native buffers.
requirements: surface must be a pointer previously returned by RGFW_createSurface.
Do not use the surface after freeing.

functions.name: RGFW_surface_freePtr
functions.description: Frees only the internal/native buffers associated with a surface, keeping the surface struct itself allocated (for use with createSurfacePtr patterns).
requirements: surface must have been initialized by RGFW_createSurfacePtr or RGFW_createSurface.
Caller manages the lifetime of the RGFW_surface struct itself.

functions.name: RGFW_loadMouse
functions.signature: RGFW_mouse* RGFW_loadMouse(u8* data, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_format format)
functions.description: Creates a custom mouse cursor from raw pixel data. Returns a backend-specific cursor handle (opaque RGFW_mouse*).
requirements: data must be a valid pixel buffer of size w×h in the given format.
w and h must be positive.
Returned handle must be freed with RGFW_freeMouse.

functions.name: RGFW_freeMouse
functions.description: Frees a mouse cursor created by RGFW_loadMouse.
requirements: mouse must be a cursor previously created by RGFW_loadMouse.
On some platforms, passing NULL is a no-op.

functions.name: RGFW_getMonitors
functions.description: Enumerates available monitors and returns a pointer to a static array of RGFW_monitor entries. Writes the number of monitors to len if non-NULL.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not free.
len may be NULL if count is not needed.

functions.name: RGFW_getPrimaryMonitor
functions.description: Returns the primary monitor’s description (position, size, refresh, scale, etc.).

functions.name: RGFW_monitor_requestMode
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_monitor_requestMode(RGFW_monitor mon, RGFW_monitorMode mode, RGFW_modeRequest request)
functions.description: Attempts to switch a monitor to a mode matching the requested parameters (resolution, refresh rate, RGB bits) per the request bitmask. Platform-dependent support.
requirements: On platforms without support, returns RGFW_FALSE.
The mon argument should originate from RGFW_getMonitors/RGFW_getPrimaryMonitor.
Only the fields indicated by request are considered.

functions.name: RGFW_monitorModeCompare
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_monitorModeCompare(RGFW_monitorMode mon, RGFW_monitorMode mon2, RGFW_modeRequest request)
functions.description: Compares two monitor modes for equivalence according to the provided request mask (scale, refresh, RGB).
requirements: Returns true if all requested aspects match; otherwise false.

functions.name: RGFW_monitor_scaleToWindow
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_monitor_scaleToWindow(RGFW_monitor mon, struct RGFW_window* win)
functions.description: Requests scaling of a monitor’s mode to match a window’s current w/h via RGFW_monitor_requestMode with RGFW_monitorScale.
requirements: win must be a valid window pointer.
Returns RGFW_TRUE if the mode switch was initiated successfully.

functions.name: RGFW_setRawMouseMode
functions.description: Globally toggles raw mouse input mode and applies it to the root window if available.
requirements: Only meaningful on platforms that support raw mouse input.
Affects subsequent mouse motion behavior and event vectors.

functions.name: RGFW_waitForEvent
functions.description: Sleeps until an event is available or the timeout elapses. On Unix uses poll with X11/Wayland fds; integrates compositor flushing on Wayland.
requirements: waitMS == 0 returns immediately; waitMS > 0 waits up to that many milliseconds; waitMS == -1 waits until next event.
Must be called from a thread initialized for the backend (after RGFW_init).

functions.name: RGFW_setQueueEvents
functions.description: Enables or disables internal queuing of events into RGFW’s FIFO event queue.
requirements: When disabled, RGFW_eventQueuePush becomes a no-op; checkEvent functions will poll if needed.

functions.name: RGFW_pollEvents
functions.description: Processes all pending backend events and updates internal state. Fills the queue if queuing is enabled.
requirements: Call regularly in your main loop to process input and window events.
Thread affinity/requirements depend on backend (e.g., Cocoa main thread).

functions.name: RGFW_stopCheckEvents
functions.description: Signals any ongoing waitForEvent loop to stop early (Unix uses a pipe signal; Windows posts a WM_NULL).
requirements: Intended to interrupt RGFW_waitForEvent or long event dispatch waits.
Backend-specific: available on all platforms with different internals.

functions.name: RGFW_checkEvent
functions.description: Pops the next event (polling first if the queue is empty and hasn’t been polled yet) and writes it to event. Returns RGFW_TRUE if an event was obtained.
requirements: event must be a valid pointer.
Use in a loop until it returns RGFW_FALSE to drain events.

functions.name: RGFW_checkQueuedEvent
functions.description: Pops the first queued event without polling the backend. Returns RGFW_TRUE if an event was present.
requirements: event must be a valid pointer.
Requires event queuing to be enabled and events in the queue.

functions.name: RGFW_isKeyPressed
functions.description: Returns true if the specified key transitioned to down this frame (edge). Uses internal keyboard state.
requirements: Call RGFW_pollEvents each frame to update states.
key must be a valid RGFW_key.

functions.name: RGFW_isKeyReleased
functions.description: Returns true if the specified key transitioned to up this frame (edge).
requirements: Requires regular event polling to populate state.

functions.name: RGFW_isKeyDown
functions.description: Returns true if the specified key is currently down (level).
requirements: Requires event polling to keep state current.

functions.name: RGFW_isMousePressed
functions.description: Returns true if the mouse button transitioned to down this frame.
requirements: Requires event polling to keep state current.
button must be a valid RGFW_mouseButton value.

functions.name: RGFW_isMouseReleased
functions.description: Returns true if the mouse button transitioned to up this frame.
requirements: Requires event polling to keep state current.

functions.name: RGFW_isMouseDown
functions.description: Returns true if the mouse button is currently pressed.
requirements: Requires event polling to keep state current.

functions.name: RGFW_getMouseScroll
functions.description: Retrieves the most recent mouse scroll delta accumulated this frame.
requirements: x and/or y may be NULL if not needed.
Call per frame after RGFW_pollEvents for freshest values.

functions.name: RGFW_getMouseVector
functions.description: Retrieves the most recent raw mouse movement vector accumulated this frame.
requirements: x and/or y may be NULL.
Depends on backend providing raw movement (or synthesized deltas).

functions.name: RGFW_createWindow
functions.signature: RGFW_window* RGFW_createWindow(const char* name, i32 x, i32 y, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_windowFlags flags)
functions.description: Creates a new window and returns its RGFW_window*. Initializes global context if needed. May also create a GL/EGL context if requested by flags.
requirements: name may be NULL (treated as empty).
w and h should be positive.
Caller must close with RGFW_window_close.
On some platforms, window creation must occur on the main thread.

functions.name: RGFW_createWindowPtr
functions.signature: RGFW_window* RGFW_createWindowPtr(const char* name, i32 x, i32 y, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_windowFlags flags, RGFW_window* win)
functions.description: Creates a new window using a caller-provided RGFW_window struct and returns it. Similar to RGFW_createWindow but avoids heap allocation for the struct.
requirements: win must be a valid pointer to writable storage for RGFW_window.
Caller must later close with RGFW_window_closePtr (or RGFW_window_close if they allocated).

functions.name: RGFW_window_createSurface
functions.signature: RGFW_surface* RGFW_window_createSurface(RGFW_window* win, u8* data, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_format format)
functions.description: Creates a surface bound to the visual/format of the specified window (important on X11) from raw pixel data.
requirements: win must be a valid window.
data must point to at least w*h*(channels) bytes.
Caller must free the returned surface with RGFW_surface_free.

functions.name: RGFW_window_createSurfacePtr
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_createSurfacePtr(RGFW_window* win, u8* data, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_format format, RGFW_surface* surface)
functions.description: Initializes a caller-provided surface against the target window’s visual/context for software blitting.
requirements: win and surface must be valid pointers.
w and h positive; data large enough for format.
Returns RGFW_TRUE on success.

functions.name: RGFW_window_blitSurface
functions.description: Blits the surface (software) onto the target window using backend-native APIs (XPutImage, wl_shm, BitBlt, etc.).
requirements: win and surface must be valid and compatible (e.g., format/visual).
Surface must have been created/initialized successfully.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getPosition
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_getPosition(RGFW_window* win, i32* x, i32* y)
functions.description: Returns the cached x/y position of the window in output parameters and RGFW_TRUE.
requirements: win must be valid.
x/y may be NULL if not needed.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getSize
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_getSize(RGFW_window* win, i32* w, i32* h)
functions.description: Returns the cached client size of the window in output parameters and RGFW_TRUE.
requirements: win must be valid.
w/h may be NULL.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getSizeInPixels
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_getSizeInPixels(RGFW_window* win, i32* w, i32* h)
functions.description: Returns the window size in physical pixels based on the monitor’s pixelRatio (HiDPI scaling).
requirements: win must be valid.
w/h may be NULL.
Relies on RGFW_window_getMonitor to compute pixel ratio.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getFlags
functions.description: Returns the internal flags bitfield associated with the window (state and options).
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getExitKey
functions.description: Returns the currently configured exit key for RGFW_window_shouldClose checks.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_setExitKey
functions.description: Sets the window’s exit key; RGFW_window_shouldClose returns true when this key is pressed.
requirements: win must be valid.
Set to RGFW_keyNULL to disable key-based close.

functions.name: RGFW_window_setEnabledEvents
functions.description: Enables the given set of events for the window (bitmask).
requirements: win must be valid.
Use RGFW_allEventFlags to enable all.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getEnabledEvents
functions.description: Returns the current enabled event mask for the window.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_setDisabledEvents
functions.description: Enables all events then disables those in the provided mask (i.e., invert behavior).
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_setEventState
functions.signature: void RGFW_window_setEventState(RGFW_window* win, RGFW_eventFlag event, RGFW_bool state)
functions.description: Directly enables or disables an event mask bit (or group).
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getUserPtr
functions.description: Returns the user pointer associated with the window (opaque client data).
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_setUserPtr
functions.description: Sets the user pointer associated with the window for client data.
requirements: win must be valid.
RGFW does not manage the lifetime of ptr.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getSrc
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the platform-specific window source structure (native handles, etc.).
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_setLayer_OSX
functions.description: macOS: Sets a custom CALayer (e.g., CAMetalLayer) on the window’s view.
requirements: Only valid on macOS; no-op elsewhere.
win must be valid; layer must be a valid Objective‑C layer object.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getView_OSX
functions.description: macOS: Returns the NSView* for the window, or NULL on non-macOS.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getWindow_OSX
functions.description: macOS: Returns the NSWindow* for the window, or NULL on non-macOS.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getHWND
functions.description: Windows: Returns the HWND for the window, or NULL on non-Windows.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getHDC
functions.description: Windows: Returns the HDC for the window, or NULL on non-Windows.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getWindow_X11
functions.description: X11: Returns the X11 Window ID for the window, or 0 if not on X11.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_getWindow_Wayland
functions.description: Wayland: Returns the wl_surface* for the window, or NULL if not on Wayland.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_setFlags
functions.description: Applies a new set of window flags, adjusting platform state accordingly (border, fullscreen, etc.).
requirements: win must be valid.
May trigger multiple platform-level operations (resize, show/hide, etc.).

functions.name: RGFW_window_checkEvent
functions.description: Like RGFW_checkEvent but filters by target window; polls if necessary and returns next event for that window.
requirements: win and event must be valid.
Use in a loop to drain per-window events.

functions.name: RGFW_window_checkQueuedEvent
functions.description: Pops the first queued event whose target matches the given window (re-queues non-matching events).
requirements: win and event must be valid.
Requires queuing enabled and queued events.

functions.name: RGFW_window_isKeyPressed
functions.description: Returns true if the key was pressed this frame and the window is in focus.
requirements: win must be valid.
Key state depends on event polling; focus gating applies.

functions.name: RGFW_window_isKeyDown
functions.description: Returns true if the key is currently down and the window is in focus.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_isKeyReleased
functions.description: Returns true if the key was released this frame and the window is in focus.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_isMousePressed
functions.description: Returns true if the mouse button pressed edge occurred this frame and the window is in focus.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_isMouseDown
functions.description: Returns true if the mouse button is currently down and the window is in focus.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_isMouseReleased
functions.description: Returns true if the mouse button released edge occurred this frame and the window is in focus.
requirements: win must be valid.

functions.name: RGFW_window_didMouseLeave
functions.description: Returns true on the first frame where the mouse left the given window during the current poll cycle.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_didMouseEnter
functions.description: Returns true on the first frame where the mouse entered the given window during the current poll cycle.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isMouseInside
functions.description: Returns true if the mouse cursor is currently inside the window bounds.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isDataDragging
functions.description: Returns true if a drag-and-drop operation is currently in progress over the window.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_getDataDrag
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_getDataDrag(RGFW_window* win, i32* x, i32* y);
functions.description: Outputs the current drag position (x,y) if a drag-and-drop operation is active over the window. Returns true if data is being dragged.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
x and y may be NULL if not needed

functions.name: RGFW_window_didDataDrop
functions.description: Returns true if a data drop (drag-and-drop) occurred on the window during the current frame.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_getDataDrop
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_getDataDrop(RGFW_window* win, const char*** files, size_t* count);
functions.description: Retrieves file paths and count from the most recent data drop on the window. Returns true if a drop occurred this frame.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
files may be NULL if not needed; on success, points to an internal array valid for the current frame
count may be NULL if not needed

functions.name: RGFW_window_close
functions.description: Closes the window and frees its RGFW_window structure. Also deletes any owned graphics contexts and may deinitialize RGFW if it was the last window.
requirements: win must be a valid RGFW_window pointer created by RGFW_createWindow or RGFW_createWindowPtr
After this call, win must not be used

functions.name: RGFW_window_closePtr
functions.description: Closes the window without freeing its RGFW_window structure. Deletes associated contexts; caller retains the RGFW_window allocation.
requirements: win must be a valid RGFW_window pointer
Caller is responsible for freeing the RGFW_window memory if allocated

functions.name: RGFW_window_move
functions.signature: void RGFW_window_move(RGFW_window* win, i32 x, i32 y);
functions.description: Moves the window to the given screen coordinates.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_moveToMonitor
functions.description: Moves the window to the specified monitor using the monitor’s work area.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
m should be a monitor previously obtained from RGFW APIs

functions.name: RGFW_window_resize
functions.signature: void RGFW_window_resize(RGFW_window* win, i32 w, i32 h);
functions.description: Resizes the window to the given dimensions.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
w and h should be positive

functions.name: RGFW_window_setAspectRatio
functions.signature: void RGFW_window_setAspectRatio(RGFW_window* win, i32 w, i32 h);
functions.description: Sets a fixed content aspect ratio for the window. On some platforms, setting both to zero clears the constraint.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
If w and h are zero on macOS/X11, aspect may be cleared

functions.name: RGFW_window_setMinSize
functions.signature: void RGFW_window_setMinSize(RGFW_window* win, i32 w, i32 h);
functions.description: Sets the minimum content size for the window.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
w and h should be non-negative

functions.name: RGFW_window_setMaxSize
functions.signature: void RGFW_window_setMaxSize(RGFW_window* win, i32 w, i32 h);
functions.description: Sets the maximum content size for the window. Passing (0,0) typically clears the constraint.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
w and h should be non-negative

functions.name: RGFW_window_focus
functions.description: Brings the window to the foreground and attempts to give it input focus.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isInFocus
functions.description: Returns true if the window is currently focused for input. Always true on WASM.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_raise
functions.description: Raises the window to the top of the stacking order. On some platforms may also re-apply fullscreen state.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_maximize
functions.description: Maximizes the window to fill available work area. Internally records previous size/position for restore.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_setFullscreen
functions.description: Toggles fullscreen mode for the window. Restores previous position and size when exiting fullscreen.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_center
functions.description: Centers the window within its monitor work area.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_minimize
functions.description: Minimizes (iconifies) the window.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_restore
functions.description: Restores the window from minimized or maximized state to its previous normal state.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_setFloating
functions.description: Toggles floating/always-on-top state for the window, if supported by the platform.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_setOpacity
functions.description: Sets the window opacity (0–255). Effect depends on platform support.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
opacity is 0–255

functions.name: RGFW_window_setBorder
functions.description: Enables or disables standard window decorations (border/titlebar).
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_borderless
functions.description: Returns true if the window is currently borderless (no decorations).
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_setDND
functions.description: Toggles drag-and-drop (DND) support for the window after creation. Note: On some platforms the RGFW_windowAllowDND flag must be set at creation for DND to function.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_allowsDND
functions.description: Returns true if the window has drag-and-drop support enabled.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_setMousePassthrough
functions.description: Enables or disables mouse input passthrough so the window no longer receives mouse events (platform-dependent).
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_setName
functions.signature: void RGFW_window_setName(RGFW_window* win, const char* name);
functions.description: Sets the window title/name shown by the OS.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
name may be NULL to set an empty title

functions.name: RGFW_window_setIcon
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_setIcon(RGFW_window* win, u8* data, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_format format);
functions.description: Sets the window icon (and taskbar icon where supported) using raw pixel data in the specified format.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
data must point to at least w*h*channels bytes (channels depend on format)
w and h must be positive

functions.name: RGFW_window_setIconEx
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_setIconEx(RGFW_window* win, u8* data, i32 w, i32 h, RGFW_format format, RGFW_icon type);
functions.description: Sets the window and/or taskbar icon(s) using raw pixel data and selects which icon(s) to set via type.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
data must point to at least w*h*channels bytes; w and h must be positive
type must be a valid RGFW_icon mask

functions.name: RGFW_window_setMouse
functions.description: Sets a custom mouse cursor on the window using a previously loaded RGFW_mouse handle.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
mouse must be a valid RGFW_mouse handle created by RGFW_loadMouse (platform-dependent)

functions.name: RGFW_window_setMouseStandard
functions.description: Sets a standard system cursor by icon type for the window.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
mouse must be a valid value of RGFW_mouseIcons

functions.name: RGFW_window_setMouseDefault
functions.description: Resets the mouse cursor to the default system pointer for the window.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_setRawMouseMode
functions.description: Enables or disables raw mouse input for the specified window, if supported by the platform.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_captureMouse
functions.description: Locks/unlocks the mouse cursor to the window (confines cursor to window region) when enabled.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_captureRawMouse
functions.description: Convenience: Enables mouse capture and raw mouse mode together when state is true; disables both when false.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_holdMouse
functions.description: Deprecated: Locks the cursor and enables raw mouse input; replaced by RGFW_window_captureRawMouse.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_unholdMouse
functions.description: Deprecated: Releases the cursor and disables raw mouse mode; replaced by RGFW_window_captureRawMouse.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isRawMouseMode
functions.description: Returns true if raw mouse mode is currently enabled for the window.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isCaptured
functions.description: Returns true if the mouse is currently captured (confined/locked) for the window.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isHoldingMouse
functions.description: Returns true if both raw mouse mode and capture are enabled (deprecated helper).
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_hide
functions.description: Hides the window from view without destroying it.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_show
functions.description: Shows the window if it is hidden. May focus depending on flags.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_flash
functions.description: Requests user attention by flashing/bouncing the window icon per request type (platform-dependent).
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
request must be a valid RGFW_flashRequest

functions.name: RGFW_window_setShouldClose
functions.description: Sets whether the window should close (affects RGFW_window_shouldClose). Setting true triggers quit event behavior.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_getGlobalMouse
functions.description: Retrieves the current global mouse cursor position in screen coordinates. Returns true on success.
requirements: x and/or y may be NULL if not needed

functions.name: RGFW_window_getMouse
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_getMouse(RGFW_window* win, i32* x, i32* y);
functions.description: Retrieves the last known mouse position relative to the window. Returns true on success.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer
x and/or y may be NULL if not needed

functions.name: RGFW_window_showMouse
functions.description: Shows or hides the mouse cursor within the window, updating internal window flags.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isMouseHidden
functions.description: Returns true if the mouse is currently hidden for the window.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_moveMouse
functions.signature: void RGFW_window_moveMouse(RGFW_window* win, i32 x, i32 y);
functions.description: Moves the mouse cursor to the specified position relative to the window (or globally, platform-dependent).
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_shouldClose
functions.description: Returns true if the window should close (close event occurred or its exit key was pressed).
requirements: win may be NULL; NULL returns true

functions.name: RGFW_window_isFullscreen
functions.description: Returns true if the window is currently in fullscreen mode.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isHidden
functions.description: Returns true if the window is currently hidden (not visible).
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isMinimized
functions.description: Returns true if the window is currently minimized/iconified.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isMaximized
functions.description: Returns true if the window is currently maximized.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_isFloating
functions.description: Returns true if the window is floating/always-on-top.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_scaleToMonitor
functions.description: Scales the window size to match its monitor’s content scale (DPI). Automatically invoked if RGFW_windowScaleToMonitor flag is used.
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_getMonitor
functions.description: Returns the monitor structure associated with the window (platform-dependent detection).
requirements: win must be a valid, initialized RGFW_window pointer

functions.name: RGFW_readClipboard
functions.description: Reads clipboard text, allocating and returning a buffer with the contents and its size through size. Caller should treat returned pointer as owned by RGFW (freed/replaced on next call).
requirements: If size is non-NULL it will be set to the number of bytes read (including trailing NUL semantics as implemented)
Returned pointer lifetime is managed by RGFW; do not free

functions.name: RGFW_readClipboardPtr
functions.description: Reads clipboard text into the provided buffer, or returns the required length if str is NULL. Returns number of bytes written/needed or negative on failure.
requirements: If str is non-NULL, strCapacity must be sufficient to hold the clipboard text plus terminator, otherwise a non-positive value may be returned
On some platforms, returning 0 or -1 indicates an error or insufficient capacity

functions.name: RGFW_writeClipboard
functions.signature: void RGFW_writeClipboard(const char* text, u32 textLen);
functions.description: Writes text to the system clipboard. Behavior varies per platform (ownership, formats, and persistence).
requirements: text must point to at least textLen bytes; text should be UTF-8
On some platforms, clipboard ownership may change on focus/selection

functions.name: RGFW_setDebugCallback
functions.description: Sets the debug callback function invoked by RGFW_sendDebugInfo. Returns the previously set callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_sendDebugInfo
functions.signature: void RGFW_sendDebugInfo(RGFW_debugType type, RGFW_errorCode err, const char* msg);
functions.description: Invokes the current debug callback (if any) with the given type, error code, and message. Also prints to stdout/stderr when RGFW_DEBUG is defined.
requirements: msg should be a valid, null-terminated string pointer (may be logged)

functions.name: RGFW_setWindowMovedCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for window move events; returns the previously registered callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setWindowResizedCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for window resize events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setWindowQuitCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for window quit events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setMousePosCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for mouse position change events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setWindowRefreshCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for window refresh (expose) events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setFocusCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for focus-in/out events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setMouseNotifyCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for mouse enter/leave notifications; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setDataDropCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for data drop (DND) events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setDataDragCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for data drag updates; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setKeyCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for key press and release events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setMouseButtonCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for mouse button press/release events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setMouseScrollCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for mouse wheel scroll events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setWindowMaximizedCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for window maximize events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setWindowMinimizedCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for window minimize events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setWindowRestoredCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for window restore events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setScaleUpdatedCallback
functions.description: Sets a global callback for DPI/content scale change events; returns the previous callback.
requirements: func may be NULL to clear the callback

functions.name: RGFW_setGlobalHints_OpenGL
functions.description: Sets the global OpenGL/EGL context creation hints pointer used by future context creations.
requirements: hints must point to a valid RGFW_glHints or be a persistent allocation for the lifetime of use

functions.name: RGFW_resetGlobalHints_OpenGL
functions.description: Resets the global OpenGL hints to default values.

functions.name: RGFW_getGlobalHints_OpenGL
functions.description: Returns the current pointer to the global OpenGL hints structure.

functions.name: RGFW_window_createContext_OpenGL
functions.description: Creates and allocates an OpenGL context for the specified window using the provided hints. Returns the new context or NULL on failure. May fall back to EGL on Wayland.
requirements: win must be a valid window
hints may be NULL to use global hints; otherwise must point to a valid RGFW_glHints

functions.name: RGFW_window_createContextPtr_OpenGL
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_createContextPtr_OpenGL(RGFW_window* win, RGFW_glContext* ctx, RGFW_glHints* hints);
functions.description: Creates an OpenGL context into a preallocated RGFW_glContext for the window. Returns true on success.
requirements: win must be valid
ctx must be a valid, writable RGFW_glContext pointer
hints may be NULL to use global hints

functions.name: RGFW_window_getContext_OpenGL
functions.description: Returns the window’s native OpenGL context pointer, or NULL if none exists or if the context is EGL-based.
requirements: win must be a valid window

functions.name: RGFW_window_deleteContext_OpenGL
functions.description: Destroys and frees an OpenGL context previously created by RGFW when owned by RGFW. If not owned, behaves like deleteContextPtr.
requirements: win must be valid
ctx must be a valid context previously associated with the window

functions.name: RGFW_window_deleteContextPtr_OpenGL
functions.description: Destroys an OpenGL context without freeing the RGFW_glContext allocation.
requirements: win must be valid
ctx must refer to a created context

functions.name: RGFW_glContext_getSourceContext
functions.description: Returns the native OpenGL context handle from an RGFW_glContext (GLX/WGL/NSOpenGL, etc.).
requirements: ctx must be valid

functions.name: RGFW_window_makeCurrentWindow_OpenGL
functions.description: Makes the window current for OpenGL rendering and tracks it as the current window in RGFW.
requirements: win may be NULL to clear current

functions.name: RGFW_window_makeCurrentContext_OpenGL
functions.description: Makes the window’s OpenGL context current on the calling thread. Pass NULL to clear current context.
requirements: win may be NULL to clear current
If switching threads, clear on the old thread first as noted in docs

functions.name: RGFW_window_swapBuffers_OpenGL
functions.description: Swaps the OpenGL buffers for the specified window.
requirements: win must have a valid current OpenGL context

functions.name: RGFW_getCurrentContext_OpenGL
functions.description: Returns the platform-native current OpenGL context handle, or NULL if none.

functions.name: RGFW_getCurrentWindow_OpenGL
functions.description: Returns the RGFW_window currently associated with the current OpenGL context via RGFW’s tracking.

functions.name: RGFW_window_swapInterval_OpenGL
functions.description: Sets the OpenGL swap interval (vsync) for the window/context, where supported.
requirements: win must be valid and have a created OpenGL context

functions.name: RGFW_getProcAddress_OpenGL
functions.description: Returns a function pointer to an OpenGL procedure by name (platform-dependent mechanism).
requirements: procname must be a null-terminated function name

functions.name: RGFW_extensionSupported_OpenGL
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_extensionSupported_OpenGL(const char* extension, size_t len);
functions.description: Checks if the given OpenGL extension string is supported in the current context.
requirements: extension must be a valid name string
len should match the name length (excluding extra trailing NULs)

functions.name: RGFW_extensionSupportedPlatform_OpenGL
functions.description: Checks whether a platform-dependent OpenGL extension is supported (e.g., GLX/WGL string query).
requirements: extension must be a valid name string
len should match the name length

functions.name: RGFW_window_createContext_EGL
functions.description: Creates and allocates an EGL context for the specified window using provided hints. Returns the new context or NULL on failure.
requirements: win must be valid
hints may be NULL to use global hints

functions.name: RGFW_window_createContextPtr_EGL
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_window_createContextPtr_EGL(RGFW_window* win, RGFW_eglContext* ctx, RGFW_glHints* hints);
functions.description: Creates an EGL context into a preallocated RGFW_eglContext for the window. Returns true on success.
requirements: win must be valid
ctx must be a valid, writable RGFW_eglContext pointer

functions.name: RGFW_window_deleteContext_EGL
functions.description: Destroys and frees an EGL context previously created by RGFW when owned by RGFW.
requirements: win must be valid
ctx must be a valid RGFW_eglContext previously associated

functions.name: RGFW_window_deleteContextPtr_EGL
functions.description: Destroys an EGL context without freeing the RGFW_eglContext allocation.
requirements: win must be valid
ctx must refer to a created EGL context

functions.name: RGFW_window_getContext_EGL
functions.description: Returns the window’s EGL context pointer, or NULL if none exists or if a native GL context is used.
requirements: win must be valid

functions.name: RGFW_getDisplay_EGL
functions.description: Returns the native EGLDisplay handle used by RGFW when EGL is loaded.

functions.name: RGFW_eglContext_getSourceContext
functions.description: Returns the native EGLContext handle from an RGFW_eglContext.
requirements: ctx must be valid

functions.name: RGFW_eglContext_getSurface
functions.description: Returns the EGLSurface handle associated with the RGFW_eglContext.
requirements: ctx must be valid

functions.name: RGFW_eglContext_wlEGLWindow
functions.description: Returns the Wayland wl_egl_window associated with the EGL context (Wayland/EGL builds).
requirements: ctx must be valid
Only meaningful on Wayland

functions.name: RGFW_window_swapBuffers_EGL
functions.description: Swaps the EGL buffers for the window’s EGL surface.
requirements: win must have a valid EGL context and surface

functions.name: RGFW_window_makeCurrentWindow_EGL
functions.description: Makes the window current for EGL and tracks it as the current window in RGFW.
requirements: win may be NULL to clear current

functions.name: RGFW_window_makeCurrentContext_EGL
functions.description: Makes the window’s EGL context current on the calling thread; pass NULL to clear.
requirements: win may be NULL to clear current

functions.name: RGFW_getCurrentContext_EGL
functions.description: Returns the current EGLContext handle, or NULL if none.

functions.name: RGFW_getCurrentWindow_EGL
functions.description: Returns the RGFW_window currently associated with the current EGL context via RGFW’s tracking.

functions.name: RGFW_window_swapInterval_EGL
functions.description: Sets the swap interval (vsync) for the current EGL context.
requirements: win must be valid and have a current EGL context

functions.name: RGFW_getProcAddress_EGL
functions.description: Returns a function pointer to an OpenGL(ES) procedure in an EGL context by name.
requirements: procname must be a null-terminated function name

functions.name: RGFW_extensionSupported_EGL
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_extensionSupported_EGL(const char* extension, size_t len);
functions.description: Checks whether an OpenGL(ES) extension is supported in the current EGL context, falling back to platform checks.
requirements: extension must be a valid name string
len should match the name length

functions.name: RGFW_extensionSupportedPlatform_EGL
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_extensionSupportedPlatform_EGL(const char* extension, size_t len);
functions.description: Checks whether a platform-dependent EGL extension is supported for the current EGLDisplay.
requirements: extension must be a valid name string
len should match the name length

functions.name: RGFW_getRequiredInstanceExtensions_Vulkan
functions.description: Returns the list of Vulkan instance extensions required by RGFW for surface creation on the active platform and sets count (typically 2).
requirements: count may be NULL if not needed

functions.name: RGFW_window_createSurface_Vulkan
functions.signature: VkResult RGFW_window_createSurface_Vulkan(RGFW_window* win, VkInstance instance, VkSurfaceKHR* surface);
functions.description: Creates a VkSurfaceKHR for the given window using the provided Vulkan instance.
requirements: win must be a valid window
instance must be a valid VkInstance
surface must be a non-NULL output pointer

functions.name: RGFW_getPresentationSupport_Vulkan
functions.signature: RGFW_bool RGFW_getPresentationSupport_Vulkan(VkInstance instance, VkPhysicalDevice physicalDevice, u32 queueFamilyIndex);
functions.description: Checks if the specified physical device and queue family support presentation for the windowing backend (X11/Wayland/etc.).
requirements: instance and physicalDevice must be valid Vulkan handles
queueFamilyIndex must be within device queue family range

functions.name: RGFW_setRootWindow
functions.description: Sets the global root (main) RGFW window pointer tracked by the library.
requirements: win may be NULL to clear the root

functions.name: RGFW_getRootWindow
functions.description: Returns the global root RGFW window pointer (may be NULL).

functions.name: RGFW_eventQueuePush
functions.description: Pushes an event into the internal event queue if queueing is enabled. May flush the queue if full (with a debug message).
requirements: event must be a valid pointer
Queueing must be enabled to store events

functions.name: RGFW_eventQueueFlush
functions.description: Clears the internal event queue without processing events.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate bytes for a generic null-terminated UTF-8/ASCII string inputs used by stubs:
# - RGFW_setClassName
# - RGFW_setXInstName
# - RGFW_createWindow / Ptr titles
# - RGFW_window_setName
# - RGFW_sendDebugInfo message
# Fuzzer harness uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times per run, typically reading from the same
# input buffer sequentially or splitting. We'll therefore generate a compact container that
# holds several null-terminated strings back-to-back to supply interesting, valid values.
#
# Design:
# - Emit N strings (2..8), each null-terminated, concatenated.
# - Include variety: ASCII simple, long names, unicode (UTF-8), edge cases (empty, spaces),
#   X11/Win class-like tokens, path-like, emoji, mixed punctuation.
# - Keep total <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic for a given seed but still varied between calls.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

CLASS_LIKE_PREFIXES = [
    "App", "Game", "Tool", "Editor", "Viewer", "Demo", "Test",
    "org.sample.", "com.example.", "io.rgfw.", "net.fuzz.", "xyz.",
]

WINDOW_TITLES = [
    "Main Window", "Preferences", "Untitled", "New Project", "Render View",
    "こんにちは",  # Japanese
    "Привет",      # Russian
    "Γειά",        # Greek
    "مرحبا",       # Arabic
    "Emoji 😀 Window",
    "Wayland/X11 Test",
    "GL/EGL Context",
    "DND & Clipboard",
    "Résumé – Café",
]

DEBUG_PHRASES = [
    "Initialization complete", "Alloc failed", "Shader compile error",
    "Connected to display", "No X11 present", "Wayland active",
    "Swap interval set", "Clipboard read/write", "Monitor scale updated",
    "Event queue flush", "Drag-and-drop received",
]

UNICODE_EXTRA = [
    "🐍 Python", "🖱️ Mouse", "⌨️ Keyboard", "🪟 Window", "🧪 Fuzz",
    "⚙️ Settings", "🎮 Game", "📦 Package", "🔧 Tools", "🧵 Thread",
]

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:+#[](){}<>|!$%&^~"  # exclude NUL


def _rand_ascii(rnd: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rnd.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _class_like(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    pref = rnd.choice(CLASS_LIKE_PREFIXES)
    body = ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 16)))
    # Ensure it looks like a class/app identifier
    return pref + body


def _title_like(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        base = rnd.choice(WINDOW_TITLES)
        if rnd.random() < 0.6:
            base += f" [{rnd.randint(1, 9999)}]"
        if rnd.random() < 0.4:
            base += " - " + rnd.choice(UNICODE_EXTRA)
        return base
    # Constructed title
    return _rand_ascii(rnd, 5, 40)


def _debug_msg(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rnd.choice(DEBUG_PHRASES)
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        base += f" (code={rnd.randint(0, 999)}, tid={rnd.randint(1, 65535)})"
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        base += "; details: " + _rand_ascii(rnd, 5, 30)
    return base


def _maybe_empty(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Some APIs accept empty titles; include occasionally
    return "" if rnd.random() < 0.3 else _rand_ascii(rnd, 1, 8)


def _assemble_strings(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Build a set of strings intended to be consumed in order by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # Order: class name, X11 inst name, window title(s), debug message(s)
    strings: List[str] = []

    # Class/instance names tend to be simple, token-like
    strings.append(_class_like(rnd))
    strings.append(_class_like(rnd) if rnd.random() < 0.7 else _maybe_empty(rnd))

    # Titles: provide multiple as different stubs may request many FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 4)):
        strings.append(_title_like(rnd))

    # Add a couple of debug messages
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        strings.append(_debug_msg(rnd))

    # Sprinkle in a path-like and a unicode-heavy string to broaden coverage
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        drive = "C:" if rnd.random() < 0.5 else "//server/share"
        strings.append(f"{drive}/Users/test/Project_{rnd.randint(1,999)}/assets/icon.png")
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        strings.append("混合-Mix-🌈-" + _rand_ascii(rnd, 3, 10))

    # Ensure total size under limit by trimming as needed
    total = sum(len(s) + 1 for s in strings)  # +1 for NULs
    if total > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Trim from the end
        out: List[str] = []
        acc = 0
        for s in strings:
            need = len(s) + 1
            if acc + need > MAX_TOTAL:
                break
            out.append(s)
            acc += need
        strings = out

    return strings


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    strings = _assemble_strings(rnd)

    # Encode as UTF-8, null-terminated segments
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    acc = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
        need = len(b) + 1
        if acc + need > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        parts.append(b + b"\x00")
        acc += need

    # As a fallback ensure at least one NUL-terminated empty string
    if not parts:
        parts = [b"\x00"]

    return b"".join(parts)

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

# Target data type: raw pixel bytes
# We must return a bytes object that fuzzer stubs will slice/repeat to fill pixel buffers.
# The stubs select width/height (1..128) and format (RGB/BGR = 3 ch, RGBA/ARGB/BGRA/ABGR = 4 ch)
# and then fill their buffers with a repeating pattern from FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
# Our job is to craft interesting yet valid pixel data patterns to exercise conversions and alpha handling.

# We will build short seeded patterns combining:
# - Solid colors (black, white, mid-gray)
# - Primary/secondary colors
# - Alpha gradients and extremes (0, 255)
# - Checkerboard and stripes
# - Ramp sequences to stress channel swizzles
# The returned bytes length stays reasonably small (<= 1024) since stubs repeat to fill.

COLORS_3 = [
    (0, 0, 0),        # black
    (255, 255, 255),  # white
    (127, 127, 127),  # gray
    (255, 0, 0),      # red
    (0, 255, 0),      # green
    (0, 0, 255),      # blue
    (255, 255, 0),    # yellow
    (0, 255, 255),    # cyan
    (255, 0, 255),    # magenta
]

COLORS_4 = [c + (255,) for c in COLORS_3] + [
    (0, 0, 0, 0),     # fully transparent
    (255, 255, 255, 0),
    (255, 0, 0, 0),
    (0, 255, 0, 0),
    (0, 0, 255, 0),
]

def pack_pixels(pixels: List[Tuple[int, ...]]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for px in pixels:
        out.extend(bytes(px))
    return bytes(out)

def mk_checkerboard(ch: int, size: int, a_values: Tuple[int, int] = (255, 255)) -> bytes:
    # size: number of pixels along one dimension in the pattern block
    # For 3 channels, ignore alpha; for 4, use supplied a_values alternating
    pixels = []
    for y in range(size):
        for x in range(size):
            on = ((x ^ y) & 1) == 0
            if ch == 3:
                c = (255, 255, 255) if on else (0, 0, 0)
            else:
                a = a_values[0] if on else a_values[1]
                c = (255, 255, 255, a) if on else (0, 0, 0, a)
            pixels.append(c)
    return pack_pixels(pixels)

def mk_stripes(ch: int, width: int, stripes: int, vertical: bool, with_alpha: bool) -> bytes:
    # Construct a small tile with colored stripes
    colors3 = COLORS_3
    colors4 = COLORS_4
    tile_h = stripes if vertical else width
    tile_w = width if vertical else stripes
    pixels: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for y in range(tile_h):
        row: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
        for x in range(tile_w):
            idx = (y if vertical else x) % (len(colors3))
            if ch == 3:
                r, g, b = colors3[idx]
                row.append((r, g, b))
            else:
                r, g, b = colors3[idx]
                a = 255 if not with_alpha else ((idx * 37) & 0xFF)
                row.append((r, g, b, a))
        pixels.extend(row)
    return pack_pixels(pixels)

def mk_ramp(ch: int, length: int, alpha_mode: str = "none") -> bytes:
    # A simple 1D gradient ramp across channels
    pixels: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for i in range(length):
        v = (i * 11) & 0xFF
        r = v
        g = (v * 3) & 0xFF
        b = (v * 5) & 0xFF
        if ch == 3:
            pixels.append((r, g, b))
        else:
            if alpha_mode == "zero_one":
                a = 0 if (i & 1) == 0 else 255
            elif alpha_mode == "ramp":
                a = (v * 7) & 0xFF
            else:
                a = 255
            pixels.append((r, g, b, a))
    return pack_pixels(pixels)

def mk_palette(ch: int, count: int) -> bytes:
    # Cycle through predefined colors
    pixels: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for i in range(count):
        if ch == 3:
            pixels.append(COLORS_3[i % len(COLORS_3)])
        else:
            c3 = COLORS_3[i % len(COLORS_3)]
            # alternate alpha extremes
            a = 0 if (i & 1) == 0 else 255
            pixels.append((c3[0], c3[1], c3[2], a))
    return pack_pixels(pixels)

def mk_interleaved_patterns(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly choose channel count 3 or 4 to bias content; actual stubs ignore this and just repeat bytes
    ch = 4 if rnd.random() < 0.6 else 3

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Header-like palette to seed a variety of bytes at the start
    parts.append(mk_palette(ch, count=16))

    # 2) Checkerboard tile with potential alpha extremes
    if ch == 4:
        a0 = rnd.choice([0, 64, 128, 192, 255])
        a1 = rnd.choice([0, 64, 128, 192, 255])
        parts.append(mk_checkerboard(4, size=4, a_values=(a0, a1)))
    else:
        parts.append(mk_checkerboard(3, size=4))

    # 3) Stripes, vertical or horizontal, with or without alpha variation
    parts.append(mk_stripes(ch, width=8, stripes=7, vertical=rnd.choice([True, False]), with_alpha=(ch == 4 and rnd.random() < 0.7)))

    # 4) Channel ramp with different alpha behavior
    alpha_mode = rnd.choice(["none", "zero_one", "ramp"]) if ch == 4 else "none"
    parts.append(mk_ramp(ch, length=17, alpha_mode=alpha_mode))

    # 5) A small random block to diversify values
    rand_len = rnd.randint(32, 96)
    rb = bytearray(rand_len)
    for i in range(rand_len):
        # favor extremes and mid values to stress conversions
        rb[i] = rnd.choice([0, 1, 15, 31, 63, 95, 127, 159, 191, 223, 239, 255])
    parts.append(bytes(rb))

    data = b"".join(parts)

    # Trim to safe size cap
    return data[:1024]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    random.seed(seed)
    # Build a composite pattern using a deterministic but varied arrangement
    data = mk_interleaved_patterns(seed ^ 0xA5A5_1234)

    # Ensure non-empty and keep within global limit (fuzzer repeats pattern)
    if not data:
        data = bytes([0, 255, 127, 63, 31, 15])

    # Final guard: limit to 4096 bytes per requirements
    return data[:4096]

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We need to generate an arbitrary byte string suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# The fuzzer stub for RGFW_writeClipboard uses:
#   std::string text = FUZZ_PARAM_STR();
#   u32 len = random within [0, text.size()]
#   RGFW_writeClipboard(text.data(), len);
# So our bytes should be interesting arbitrary data; the stub will choose a length.
# We'll craft diverse patterns: UTF-8 sequences, NULs, long repeats, ASCII, emoji,
# mixed encodings, and edge-case lengths. Keep <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_ascii = b"".join(bytes([c]) for c in range(32, 127))  # printable ASCII
_controls = bytes(range(0, 32)) + b"\x7f"  # control chars incl. DEL

# Some useful UTF-8 sequences including multi-byte code points
_utf8_samples = [
    "".encode("utf-8"),
    "a".encode("utf-8"),
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog".encode("utf-8"),
    "こんにちは世界".encode("utf-8"),
    "😀😃😄😁😆😅😂🤣☺️😊".encode("utf-8"),
    "Русский текст".encode("utf-8"),
    "العربية".encode("utf-8"),
    "हिन्दी".encode("utf-8"),
    "עברית".encode("utf-8"),
    "한국어".encode("utf-8"),
    "προγραμμα".encode("utf-8"),
]

# Sequences with embedded NULs and varying strides
_def_nully = [
    b"\x00",
    b"\x00" * 16,
    (b"AB\x00CD" * 8),
]

# Byte ramps and patterns
_patterns: List[bytes] = [
    bytes(range(256)),
    bytes(reversed(range(256))),
    (_ascii + b"\n") * 4,
    _controls * 4,
    b"\xff\xfe\xfd\xfc" * 64,
    b"\x00\xff" * 256,
]

# Random chunk generator helpers

def rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def make_chunk(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a chunk type
    choice = rng.randrange(10)
    if choice == 0:
        # UTF-8 sample (maybe truncated or repeated)
        base = rng.choice(_utf8_samples)
        if not base:
            return base
        reps = 1 + rng.randrange(1, max(2, min(8, budget // max(1, len(base)))))
        chunk = (base * reps)[:budget]
        return chunk
    elif choice == 1:
        # ASCII range with newlines and tabs
        line = b"".join([
            b"ASCII:",
            b" ",
            _ascii,
            b"\n\tEND\n",
        ])
        return line[:budget]
    elif choice == 2:
        # Controls
        return (_controls + b"\x00\x01\x02\x03")[:budget]
    elif choice == 3:
        # Null-heavy pattern
        return rng.choice(_def_nully)[:budget]
    elif choice == 4:
        # Structured header + payload style
        # Compose a faux binary blob: magic + length + payload
        magic = rng.choice([b"RGFW", b"CLIP", b"DATA", b"\x89BIN"])
        pay_len = max(0, min(budget - len(magic) - 4, rng.randrange(0, max(1, budget - len(magic) - 4))))
        payload = rand_bytes(rng, pay_len)
        return magic + struct.pack("<I", pay_len) + payload
    elif choice == 5:
        # Incrementing or decrementing ramp
        base = rng.choice(_patterns)
        reps = 1 + rng.randrange(1, max(2, min(16, budget // max(1, len(base)))))
        return (base * reps)[:budget]
    elif choice == 6:
        # Repeated single byte
        bval = rng.randrange(256)
        return bytes([bval]) * min(budget, rng.randrange(1, max(2, budget + 1)))
    elif choice == 7:
        # Mixed UTF-8 and NULs
        s = rng.choice(_utf8_samples)
        mix = []
        for _ in range(rng.randrange(4, 16)):
            mix.append(s)
            mix.append(b"\x00" * rng.randrange(0, 4))
            mix.append(rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(0, 4)))
        chunk = b"".join(mix)
        return chunk[:budget]
    elif choice == 8:
        # Length-prefixed ASCII segment
        word = rng.choice([b"hello", b"world", b"clipboard", b"rgfw", b"test", b"utf8"])
        reps = rng.randrange(1, 64)
        data = (word + b" ") * reps
        return struct.pack("<I", len(data)) + data[:max(0, budget - 4)]
    else:
        # Pure random
        return rand_bytes(rng, min(budget, rng.randrange(0, max(1, budget + 1))))


def diversify_edges(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # A set of small edge-case strings to prepend/append
    return [
        b"",  # empty
        b"\x00",  # single NUL
        b"\n",  # newline
        b"\r\n",  # CRLF
        b"\xef\xbb\xbf",  # UTF-8 BOM
        b"\x00\x00\x00\x00",  # zeros
        b"END\0",  # text with embedded NUL
        b"\xf0\x9f\x98\x80",  # 😀
    ]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide total size within a sensible range; stub will pick used length.
    # Favor a spread across tiny, small, medium, and larger buffers.
    size_class = rng.random()
    if size_class < 0.15:
        total = rng.randrange(0, 32)
    elif size_class < 0.45:
        total = rng.randrange(32, 256)
    elif size_class < 0.85:
        total = rng.randrange(256, 1024)
    else:
        total = rng.randrange(1024, min(4096, 3072))

    total = max(0, min(MAX_TOTAL, total))

    # Build the buffer from several chunks
    buf = bytearray()

    # Optionally start with an edge prefix
    edges = diversify_edges(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.6 and edges:
        prefix = rng.choice(edges)
        buf.extend(prefix[: max(0, total - len(buf))])

    # Fill with chunks until reaching the target size
    while len(buf) < total:
        budget = total - len(buf)
        if budget <= 0:
            break
        chunk = make_chunk(rng, budget)
        if not chunk and budget > 0:
            # Ensure progress
            chunk = rand_bytes(rng, min(8, budget))
        buf.extend(chunk[:budget])

    # Optionally append an edge suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.6 and edges and len(buf) < MAX_TOTAL:
        suffix_budget = min(MAX_TOTAL - len(buf), rng.randrange(0, 16))
        if suffix_budget > 0:
            suffix = rng.choice(edges)
            buf.extend(suffix[:suffix_budget])

    # Ensure final size limit
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        del buf[MAX_TOTAL:]

    return bytes(buf)
